variants.title: User updates profile and refreshes immediately
variants.context: The primary database accepts a profile update, but a read goes to a replica that is still stale.
variants.constraint: Replication is asynchronous and users expect freshness.
variants.question: What keeps the experience correct?
variants.expectedPattern: Read-your-own-writes logic for that user or a short freshness window on their reads.
wrongChoices: Block all reads until replication catches up
Disable replicas
Set a long TTL

variants.title: Follower lags behind leader
variants.context: A replica is behind and serves the old version of a post while the author refreshed the page.
variants.constraint: The rest of the system accepts eventual consistency.
variants.question: Which read behavior is appropriate?
variants.expectedPattern: Read the author’s writes from the primary or a fresh path.
wrongChoices: Force all reads to wait on the leader
Use CDN caches for everything
Ignore the freshness issue

variants.title: Regional failover creates stale data
variants.context: A user in a secondary region reads a profile while failover is happening and sees old data.
variants.constraint: Some replicas are behind during failover.
variants.question: What is the right system behavior?
variants.expectedPattern: Use lag-aware routing and a freshness policy for critical reads.
wrongChoices: Always read from the zone with the most replicas
Disable the failover region
Tell users to retry

variants.title: Order status appears stale after update
variants.context: The user updates order status, then reads the order immediately and sees an older state.
variants.constraint: The system is eventually consistent but needs better user experience.
variants.question: What is the correct tradeoff?
variants.expectedPattern: Provide fresh reads for the same user session or user-specific workflow.
wrongChoices: Explain the lag to the user
Make all users wait for strong consistency
Use a read-only API

variants.title: User sees stale post after comment
variants.context: A user submits a comment and sees a stale thread because the read route goes to a non-authoritative replica.
variants.constraint: The app is optimized for availability and throughputs.
variants.question: How do you preserve trust?
variants.expectedPattern: Sessions or user identity should use a fresh read path for recent writes.
wrongChoices: No read-your-own-writes rule
Long timeouts on writes
Move all writes to the edge

variants.title: Global reads feel inconsistent
variants.context: Users in different regions do not see the same state at the same timestamp.
variants.constraint: The system is distributed and sync is not instant.
variants.question: What is the core principle?
variants.expectedPattern: Eventual consistency is acceptable if the system makes freshness guarantees explicit for the active user and critical flows.
wrongChoices: All reads must be fully global strong consistency
No consistency model is needed
All data must be in one region

variants.title: User deletion reads stale content
variants.context: A user deletes a post and immediately reloads a page that still shows it on a follower.
variants.constraint: Deletion and visibility updates are asynchronous.
variants.question: How do you avoid the bug?
variants.expectedPattern: Use a freshness-aware read path and metadata-based invalidation for the actor’s own actions.
wrongChoices: Ignore stale reads
Keep deletes in a queue only
Wait for global sync before deletion is visible

variants.title: Cached profile update appears one minute later
variants.context: Users update profile preferences and still see the old page for a minute because the cache is serving an older value.
variants.constraint: The cache is valid but the user wants immediate freshness.
variants.question: What is the right compromise?
variants.expectedPattern: Invalidate or refresh the cache for that user immediately and keep a bounded TTL for others.
wrongChoices: Never expire the cache
Always bypass the cache
Do nothing and tell users to refresh

variants.title: Social feed shows outdated items
variants.context: An item is posted and appears on the feed of the posting user only after a delay.
variants.constraint: The system balances availability and replica lag.
variants.question: How do you handle the user expectation?
variants.expectedPattern: Ensure the writer sees the post immediately from a fresh source while followers accept eventual consistency.
wrongChoices: Update all replicas before the feed is visible
Block writes until all region replicas sync
Ignore the lag as acceptable for all users

variants.title: Web app modifies account settings in one region
variants.context: The user edits a setting, then reads the account page from another region and sees a stale value.
variants.constraint: Regional consistency is eventually convergent but not instant.
variants.question: What is the honest design answer?
variants.expectedPattern: Use a bounded freshness policy for the active user and explain that global equality is not guaranteed instantly.
wrongChoices: Promise strong consistency globally
Do nothing and accept stale reads
Lock the platform on every write

variants.title: Cart item vanishes after add
variants.context: A shopper adds an item, then the cart widget reads from a replica and shows zero items.
variants.constraint: The add already committed on the primary.
variants.question: What read policy belongs on the cart?
variants.expectedPattern: Sticky or primary reads for the shopper’s recent cart writes.
wrongChoices: Always read carts from the farthest replica
Delay the add until every replica acknowledges
Hide the cart until the next day

variants.title: Password change then login fails
variants.context: The user changes a password, is redirected to login, and authentication still checks a stale replica.
variants.constraint: Auth cannot accept a lag window for that user.
variants.question: Where must the login read go?
variants.expectedPattern: Read credentials from the primary (or a synchronously confirmed replica) after a password write.
wrongChoices: Authenticate against any replica immediately
Cache the old password hash at the edge
Ask the user to wait five minutes without a fresh path

variants.title: Monotonic reads broken on mobile
variants.context: A timeline first shows a new tweet, then an older timeline after a replica switch.
variants.constraint: Users notice time going backwards.
variants.question: Which session guarantee is missing?
variants.expectedPattern: Monotonic reads: once a client has seen version N, later reads in that session must not go backwards.
wrongChoices: Random replica on every scroll
Global linearizability for every follower
No version tokens on the client

variants.title: Like count jumps then drops
variants.context: The author sees 101 likes from the primary, then 97 from a replica on refresh.
variants.constraint: Counters are eventually consistent.
variants.question: How do you keep the author’s view stable?
variants.expectedPattern: Pin the author’s reads to a fresh source or show a monotonic client-side count until replicas catch up.
wrongChoices: Show replica counts immediately after a write
Stop counting likes
Lock the entire likes table globally

variants.title: Multi-tab edit conflict
variants.context: Two browser tabs load the same document from different replicas and last-write-wins silently drops a paragraph.
variants.constraint: Collaborative edits need conflict detection.
variants.question: What consistency tool belongs here?
variants.expectedPattern: Version tokens or optimistic concurrency so stale writes are rejected or merged.
wrongChoices: Last write always wins with no version check
Force all edits through one replica without versions
Disable saving

variants.title: Causal order of comments
variants.context: A reply appears before the parent comment because replicas apply writes out of order.
variants.constraint: Conversation threads need happens-before order.
variants.question: What ordering guarantee is required?
variants.expectedPattern: Causal consistency so a reply is not visible before its parent in the same thread.
wrongChoices: Any replica apply order is fine
Strong global order for unrelated posts
Hide all comments until world-wide sync

variants.title: Inventory decrement vs browse
variants.context: Checkout decrements stock on the primary; the product page still shows “in stock” from a replica.
variants.constraint: Overselling is worse than a slightly empty-looking page.
variants.question: Which path needs stronger reads?
variants.expectedPattern: Critical stock checks at checkout read from the primary; browse can stay eventually consistent.
wrongChoices: Both browse and checkout always use the most lagged replica
Strong consistency on every marketing page
Never decrement stock

variants.title: Session token after logout
variants.context: Logout invalidates a token on the primary, but a replica still accepts it for 20 seconds.
variants.constraint: Security-sensitive reads cannot be stale.
variants.question: What is the right invalidation model?
variants.expectedPattern: Synchronous invalidation or primary reads for authz checks, plus short-lived tokens.
wrongChoices: Eventual logout is acceptable for session tokens
Cache valid tokens at the CDN for an hour
Only delete the cookie in the browser

variants.title: Leader election split brain
variants.context: Two primaries accept writes during a network partition and later diverge.
variants.constraint: The cluster must choose one history.
variants.question: What consistency property was violated?
variants.expectedPattern: Single-leader (or consensus) so only one primary can accept writes in a partition.
wrongChoices: Allow two writable primaries and merge later blindly
Turn off health checks
Read from any node as if it were primary

variants.title: Bounded staleness SLA
variants.context: A dashboard promises data no older than 5 seconds, but replica lag is 40 seconds.
variants.constraint: The SLA is a product requirement.
variants.question: How should the read router behave?
variants.expectedPattern: Reject or reroute reads when replica lag exceeds the freshness bound, falling back to a fresher replica or primary.
wrongChoices: Serve any replica regardless of lag
Hide the lag metric
Change the SLA after the page loads
